identity.name: Intel executive leadership (CEO and capital-allocation officers), 2024-2025

goals.goal: Preserve leading-edge manufacturing capability while ending the cash burn
Convert fixed capital obligations into variable ones until external foundry demand is contracted
Protect the balance sheet from a second shock that would foreclose the manufacturing strategy
Keep Foundry financeable as a separate entity rather than a captive cost centre

fears: Being contractually bound to spend tens of billions on capacity with no buyer (FACT-003)
Irreversibility: commitments that cannot be unwound when demand does not arrive
A second loss event on the scale of Q3 2024 forcing retreat from manufacturing altogether (FACT-005)
Being read in Berlin and Brussels as an unreliable partner

factions.name: Technology / foundry bloc
factions.goal: Build capacity ahead of demand; commitments follow a credible roadmap
factions.veto_scope: can declare a node not ready, which blocks any fab decision

factions.name: Finance and treasury
factions.goal: Gate every commitment; rank by sunk-cost asymmetry and cash payback

factions.name: Product / client CPU bloc
factions.goal: Return cash to product lines; treat foundry capex as a drag

factions.name: Board of directors
factions.goal: No second balance-sheet shock; protect state and CHIPS relationships

decision_rule: No new greenfield wafer capacity without binding external customer commitments covering most of output; irreversible commitments require board sign-off and are ranked by sunk-cost asymmetry, so funded and politically load-bearing US sites go first and unfunded EU sites last.

resources.resource: Sunk US capacity (Arizona, Oregon, New Mexico, Ohio)
Paused Magdeburg site as an option
resources.magnitude: low carrying cost, high political cost

constraints.constraint: Cash position and loss trajectory prohibit new multi-billion fixed commitments
German aid is milestone- and site-conditioned; restart is a re-application, not a resumption
Land, utility and supplier commitments at Magdeburg carry exit cost
Cancellation damages credibility with the Commission and the federal government
US sites are already funded and politically load-bearing, so they outrank Germany

options.action: Pause German and Polish projects by about two years (executed 2024-09)
Retain the Magdeburg land and permits as a dormant option
Offer advanced packaging or a later node instead of the announced wafer fab
Bring in a co-investor or JV partner for European capacity
Separate Intel Foundry into an independent subsidiary to widen financing options

ruled_out.reason: No customer commitments to fill it; converts variable cost into fixed obligation at the worst point in the loss cycle

ruled_out.action: Hold the option open indefinitely while signalling full commitment
ruled_out.reason: Carries political expectation, audit scrutiny and land cost with no decision value

ruled_out.action: Commit to any additional EU greenfield site
ruled_out.reason: Same defect as Magdeburg; would forfeit the credibility of the demand-based rationale

ruled_out.action: Pay the EUR 9.9bn back as a penalty framed as damages
ruled_out.reason: Accepts a liability characterisation that invites further claims

reaction_function.if: Berlin offers a larger aid package or an equity stake to keep the site alive
reaction_function.then: Intel does not restart the wafer fab; it offers packaging or a later node and keeps the land
reaction_function.because: The constraint is demand, not subsidy size

reaction_function.if: Berlin demands return of the EUR 9.9bn
reaction_function.then: Intel negotiates against documented sunk cost and refuses any payment characterised as damages
reaction_function.because: Accepting a penalty framing invites further claims

reaction_function.if: The Commission opens a state-aid recovery procedure
reaction_function.then: Intel argues demand collapse rather than opportunism and settles rather than litigates
reaction_function.because: Litigation is a distraction it cannot afford

reaction_function.if: A lead external customer signs a binding 18A/14A volume commitment
reaction_function.then: The constraint eases but Ohio and Arizona absorb the capacity first

beliefs_about.belief: External foundry demand never materialised at the scale the 2022 announcement assumed
Berlin will prioritise not appearing to have been taken in, and will convert the loss into a domestic political asset

beliefs_about.about: German federal government's model of Intel
beliefs_about.belief: Berlin reads the cancellation as a negotiating squeeze for more subsidy; that reading is wrong

falsifiers: Intel recommits capital to Magdeburg, or to any new EU greenfield wafer fab, before 2027
Intel sustains Ohio and Arizona funding at planned pace while continuing to cite demand insufficiency
A binding large external foundry customer signs and Intel still declines to revisit European capacity
premises_missing: Intel's actual capex commitments to Magdeburg at cancellation, and any contractual break cost
The aid agreement terms: clawback clauses, milestone definitions, whether the EUR 9.9bn was disbursed
Any US government equity or quasi-equity position in Intel during 2025
The share of 18A/14A capacity already contracted to external customers by mid-2025
